characters.continuity: Raimi Spider-Man universe Flint Marko as he appears in the MCU film Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021); only No Way Home events are used
characters.summary: Flint Marko turns his body into sand and controls it: he can harden, compact, disperse or reshape it, whip it into sandstorms, absorb nearby sand to grow into a giant sand figure, and fly as a sandstorm. In No Way Home he first helps Spider-Man against Electro, then turns on the Spider-Men at the Statue of Liberty until he is cured back to human form.

mechanisms: Disperses into sand or becomes intangible
Heals by reabsorbing sand (reformed after Electro's crane blast severed his giant arm and head)

weaknesses: Sandman's Cure: activating the cure on him reverted his sand body to flesh and bone and ended the fight
mobility: Escapes through gaps by dispersing into sand
limitations: His sand form was stuck: he could not return to human form until he was cured

sources.supports: MCU Wiki: Sandman's powers and his No Way Home events (Electro fight in the forest, escape, Liberty Island giant form, being cured)

feats.claim: Shielded Spider-Man from Electro's bolt by becoming a wall of sand, then trapped Electro in a sand typhoon.
Grew into a gigantic sand figure at the Statue of Liberty, grabbed Spider-Man in mid-air with a giant fist, and flooded the statue's crown with sand.
Reformed after Electro's crane blast severed his giant arm and head.

notableResults.citation: Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021)
notableResults.note: Team win with Spider-Man in the forest. Sandman trapped Electro in a sand typhoon while Spider-Man destroyed the poles feeding his power, and Electro was taken to the Sanctum cells.

notableResults.citation: Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021)
notableResults.note: Liberty Island. His giant form chased them and engulfed an older Spider-Man, but that Spider-Man's free hand activated the cure, and Marko reverted to human form.

conditional.ability: Growth to a gigantic sand form

campaignTags.claim: Absorbs sand to grow into a gigantic sand figure (Liberty Island).
Can fly as a sandstorm; flew away over the authorities after escaping Happy Hogan's condo.
Heals by reabsorbing sand; reformed after his giant arm and head were severed.

unknowns: Exact limits on the volume of sand he can control.
Water weakness (seen in the Raimi films) is not shown in No Way Home or on the MCU Wiki page, so it was removed.
Exact height of the giant form is not documented (no giant-sized tag).

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe, Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)
characters.summary: Corrupted by the Darkhold and convinced her sons exist in other universes, Wanda hunts America Chavez for her multiversal power. She besieges Kamar-Taj, dreamwalks into her Earth-838 counterpart and kills the Illuminati, using chaos magic, hex bolts, psychic attacks and mind control, until seeing her sons' fear makes her destroy every Darkhold at Mount Wundagore at the cost of her life.

techniques: Chaos magic erasure and warping (erased Black Bolt's mouth, warped Mister Fantastic)
Psychic attack (snapped Professor X's neck within his mind)
Energy absorption (absorbed Captain Marvel's cosmic energy)

mechanisms: Took a cannon blast at Kamar-Taj and kept fighting
Overpowered Professor X inside her own mind

weaknesses: Destroying the Darkhold copy she uses breaks her dreamwalk and returns her to her own body (Sara at Kamar-Taj)
Her sons' rejection: seeing Tommy and Billy fear her made her abandon her plan
mobility: Teleports in a trail of red smoke
limitations: Dreamwalking depends on the Darkhold ritual; the possession ends if the book is destroyed
characters.formDifferences: Darkhold-corrupted and openly lethal: she gains Darkhold dreamwalking into a multiversal counterpart and kills where earlier Wanda did not, while keeping her chaos magic, flight and mind control.

sources.supports: MCU Wiki: Wanda's Darkhold corruption, the Siege of Kamar-Taj, dreamwalking, the Illuminati attack, flight, teleportation, mind control, and her end at Mount Wundagore

feats.claim: While possessing her Earth-838 counterpart, killed the Illuminati: erased Black Bolt's mouth, warped Mister Fantastic into strands, threw Captain Carter's shield back through her, and dropped a statue on Captain Marvel after absorbing her energy.
feats.citation: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)

feats.claim: Besieged Kamar-Taj alone, survived a cannon blast, brought down a building, and breached the protective barrier with hex bolts after mind-controlling a sorcerer.
feats.citation: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)

feats.claim: Destroyed every Darkhold in the multiverse and the Darkhold Castle on Mount Wundagore.
feats.citation: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)

notableResults.citation: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)
notableResults.note: He entered her mind to free her counterpart; she overpowered him there and snapped his neck psychically.

notableResults.citation: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)
notableResults.note: Erased his mouth with chaos magic, so his own voice killed him.

notableResults.citation: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)
notableResults.note: Warped him into rubber strands and his head exploded.

notableResults.citation: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)
notableResults.note: Caught her shield and threw it back, cutting her in half.

notableResults.citation: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)
notableResults.note: Absorbed her cosmic energy, then dropped a statue on her.

notableResults.citation: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)
notableResults.note: Siege of Kamar-Taj: swatted Strange aside, knocked out Wong and seized America Chavez.

notableResults.citation: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)
notableResults.note: At Mount Wundagore, Chavez punched her through portals to Earth-838, where her sons' fear made her give up.

conditional.dependsOn: The Darkhold; a copy's destruction broke the ritual, and she resumed it with the original at Mount Wundagore

campaignTags.claim: Casts Darkhold rituals (dreamwalking) and chaos-magic spells such as hex bolts.
Uses the Darkhold spellbook to dreamwalk.
Flies by propelling herself with psionic blasts (to Kamar-Taj, Mount Wundagore and Illuminati HQ).
Appears and vanishes in a trail of red smoke.
Mind-controlled a Kamar-Taj sorcerer and forced America Chavez to open portals.

unknowns: Her apparent death under the collapsing Darkhold Castle on Mount Wundagore; the MCU Wiki says a red burst of magic killed her.

characters.id: mcu:Scarlet Witch|House of M Scarlet Witch
characters.continuity: Marvel Comics, House of M (2005) event (Earth-58163 reality created by Earth-616 Wanda Maximoff). Comics form only; not shown in the MCU.
characters.summary: During her breakdown, Wanda reshaped reality into the House of M, a world ruled by mutants. When the heroes restored their memories and moved against her, she ended that world with three words, "No more mutants," which depowered most of the world's mutants (the Decimation).

mechanisms: Hawkeye's arrow disintegrated on contact with her

weaknesses: Emotionally driven: distress over her family (seeing Pietro dead at Magnus's hands) triggered her uncontrolled, world-ending spell
mobility: Not established in the sources reviewed
limitations: Prone to mental breakdowns, catatonic states and recurring loss of her powers
characters.formDifferences: Reality-scale chaos magic at the height of her breakdown: she rewrites the whole world and strips mutant powers worldwide, far beyond her usual hexes.

sources.supports: Marvel Database: Wanda in the House of M reality; Hawkeye's attack, "No More Mutants" ending (House of M #6-7)
Marvel Database: she reshaped reality into House of M, the Decimation, her chaos magic, breakdowns and power loss

feats.claim: Reshaped reality into the House of M, a world where mutants ruled.
Said "No more mutants" and depowered most of the world's mutants (the Decimation).

notableResults.citation: House of M #7 (2005)
notableResults.note: Hawkeye shot an arrow at her; it disintegrated on contact, and her sons erased him from existence.

campaignTags.claim: Warps reality with chaos magic on a planetary scale.

unknowns: Exact trigger mechanisms for her breakdowns.
The original claim of a win over the combined Avengers and X-Men in House of M #1 was not supported as a fight on the pages opened and was removed.
Flight and "probability shielding" were not documented and were removed.

characters.continuity: Marvel Comics, Earth-616 (Wundagore Mountain origin; Chthon's possession of Wanda in Avengers #187). Comics form only; not MCU. The MCU's Wundagore material belongs to the Darkhold Scarlet Witch record.
characters.summary: Wanda's link to Wundagore Mountain, where the High Evolutionary altered her as an infant and the Elder God Chthon is imprisoned. The mountain's energies gave her a latent talent for magic, which Agatha Harkness trained. Chthon infused her as an infant and later possessed her at Wundagore, using her body against the Avengers until they exorcised him.

mechanisms: Not established in the sources reviewed

weaknesses: Susceptible to possession by Chthon, who infused her as an infant and used her as a vessel at Wundagore
mobility: Not established in the sources reviewed
limitations: Chthon twice suppressed her mutant hex power; she suffers recurring power loss and breakdowns
characters.formDifferences: Wundagore-rooted Wanda: her magic comes from Wundagore's energies and Chthon's infusion and is trained as witchcraft under Agatha Harkness, and it is open to Chthon's possession, unlike the MCU's Darkhold-driven form.

sources.supports: Marvel Database: Wundagore origin, Chthon's influence and possessions, training with Agatha Harkness, chaos magic, power loss
Marvel Database: Avengers #187, Chthon possessing Wanda at Wundagore and the Avengers' exorcism

feats.claim: While possessed by Chthon, paralyzed Wonder Man with a spell and knocked out the Wasp with an arcane bolt; Chthon in her body was "more than a match" for the Avengers.
After the exorcism, used a hex bolt to set off an avalanche that buried the marionette holding Chthon's essence.

notableResults.opponent: Avengers (Captain America, Ms. Marvel, Falcon, Wasp, Wonder Man, Quicksilver)
notableResults.citation: Avengers #187 (1979)
notableResults.note: Chthon, possessing Wanda, held off the team until the Beast seized the Darkhold and the Avengers' combined will pushed Chthon out into Django Maximoff's marionette.

conditional.ability: Chthon's possession and power through her
conditional.dependsOn: Wundagore Mountain, where Chthon's spirit is bound

campaignTags.claim: Trained in witchcraft ("true magic") by Agatha Harkness; casts hexes and spells.

unknowns: No form actually named "Scarlet Witch of Wundagore" is documented on the pages opened. The roster name may mean the MCU's Wundagore-throne Scarlet Witch (already covered by the Darkhold record) or this comics Wundagore/Chthon material. The owner should decide.
The original feat about repelling demons with Wundagore's energy (Avengers #187) and the win over Agatha Harkness (Avengers #128) were not supported and were removed.
Flight is not documented on the pages opened.

characters.summary: Bob Reynolds, an addict who volunteered for Valentina de Fontaine's secret Sentry experiment in Malaysia, came out of it with godlike power: believed stronger than all the Avengers combined, bulletproof and able to fly. Recast as the Sentry, he easily overpowered the Thunderbolts, then turned on de Fontaine until her failsafe released his alter ego, the Void.
weaknesses: A failsafe kill switch built into him; Mel triggered it and incapacitated him
limitations: Unstable psyche: his power feeds his delusions of grandeur, and incapacitating him released the Void

sources.supports: Thunderbolts* (Wikipedia via Wikiwand): Bob's origin, powers, overpowering the Thunderbolts, the kill switch and the Void
High On Films ending explainer: bullets fail to harm him, he levitates, he overpowers the team at the Watchtower, Mel's kill switch

feats.claim: Drew enemy fire so Yelena, Walker and Ghost could escape.
Was shot at the O.X.E. facility and came away unharmed.
Easily overpowered the assembled Thunderbolts at the Watchtower, then spared them as no threat.

notableResults.opponent: Thunderbolts (Yelena Belova, Bucky Barnes, John Walker, Red Guardian, Ghost)
notableResults.citation: Thunderbolts* (2025)
notableResults.note: At the Watchtower, on de Fontaine's orders; he chose not to kill them.

campaignTags.claim: Rises and levitates into the sky under his own power.

unknowns: The MCU Wiki Sentry page could not be loaded (site error), so the film's full power set (for example energy projection or molecular powers) is not documented here.
The comics feats in the original record (tearing Carnage in half, Absorbing Man) were removed as non-MCU.

characters.continuity: Marvel Comics, Earth-616, Uncanny Avengers (Vol. 1, 2012-2014) Apocalypse Twins arc. Comics form only; not MCU.
characters.summary: The Apocalypse Twins resurrected Robert Reynolds with both a Life Seed and a Death Seed and made him one of their Horsemen of Death, alongside Banshee, Grim Reaper and Daken. His madness grew until he saw himself as Apocalypse's heir. He ambushed Thor on another world and later fought Wasp and Thor at the Twins' Tachyon Dam.

mechanisms: Not established for this form in the sources reviewed

limitations: Increasing madness after his resurrection; came to see himself as Apocalypse's heir
characters.formDifferences: Resurrected by the Apocalypse Twins with a Life Seed and a Death Seed as a Horseman of Death. He serves the Twins' cause and turns hostile to mutants, which he called "cancerous", rather than acting as a hero.

sources.supports: Marvel Database: Death Seed resurrection as a Horseman of Death, the Thor ambush on Tyconria, Tachyon Dam, Exitar (Uncanny Avengers #9-22)

feats.claim: Took Thor by surprise on the lava planet Tyconria and briefly subdued him.
feats.citation: Uncanny Avengers #15 (as cited by Marvel Database)

notableResults.citation: Uncanny Avengers #15 (as cited by Marvel Database)
notableResults.note: He briefly subdued Thor on Tyconria. Thor later returned and joined Wasp against him at the Tachyon Dam, and the page gives no final result.

conditional.ability: Resurrected existence as a Horseman of Death
conditional.dependsOn: The Apocalypse Twins' Life Seed and Death Seed

campaignTags.claim: Flies; Marvel Database cites his flight during the Horseman arc (Uncanny Avengers #10).

unknowns: The original feat "tore a Celestial apart" (Uncanny Avengers #11) is not supported. The page says only that he planned to move a Celestial body away from Earth (#22), not that he did.
The "celestial durability" and "instantaneous regeneration" claims and the cosmic-anchor limitation were not documented and were removed.
Issue numbers were read from Marvel Database footnotes through a summarizer and may be slightly off.

characters.summary: The Void is Bob Reynolds' destructive alter ego, embodying his depression and insecurities. It was released when Mel triggered Sentry's kill switch. It engulfed New York in darkness, turned people into shadows and trapped them in pocket dimensions built from their worst memories, until the Thunderbolts' belief in Bob let him regain control.

techniques: Trapping victims in pocket dimensions of their worst memories

mechanisms: Overwhelmed the Thunderbolts inside the darkness

weaknesses: Bob himself: when the team affirmed their belief in him, he regained control and the Void was extinguished
mobility: Not established in the sources reviewed
limitations: Exists as Bob's repressed alter ego and emerged only after the kill switch incapacitated Sentry
characters.formDifferences: The Void is Bob's dark alter ego, not the golden Sentry brawler. It works through supernatural darkness that swallows New York and traps people in their own trauma, rather than through physical blows.

sources.supports: Thunderbolts* (Wikipedia via Wikiwand): the Void's origin, darkness over New York, pocket dimensions, shadows, and its defeat
High On Films ending explainer: the kill switch unleashing the Void, citizens trapped in pocket dimensions, the Void overwhelming the team, Bob regaining control

feats.claim: Engulfed New York City in darkness, trapping citizens in pocket dimensions built from their worst memories.
Quickly overwhelmed the Thunderbolts when they entered the darkness.

notableResults.citation: Thunderbolts* (2025)
notableResults.note: The Void overpowered them, but they rallied around Bob instead of fighting; he regained control and light returned to the city.

conditional.dependsOn: Sentry being incapacitated (Mel's failsafe kill switch)

unknowns: The original record described the comics Void (Siege #2 killing Ares, Siege #4 death at Thor's hands, a giant monstrous form). Because the Void appears in the MCU, the record was rebuilt from Thunderbolts*, and those comics feats were removed.
Whether the Void flies or changes size in the film is not documented in the sources opened.
How far the pocket dimensions reach, and whether the shadow-turned people are physically relocated, is not documented in detail.
teleports-others tag not applied (reviewer): the sources say victims are pulled into shadow pocket dimensions, but do not establish physical transport of others; revisit with a fuller film source.

characters.summary: An immortal Eternal who transmutes the matter she touches, turning a bus into rose petals, pavement into sand and a tree into water. She was thought unable to change sentient beings until she turned a Deviant into a tree. Through the Uni-Mind she turned the Celestial Tiamut to stone and stopped the Emergence.
weaknesses: Reluctant to kill: she hesitated to use her powers on Tiamut
mobility: No flight; she only levitated a few feet while in the Uni-Mind
limitations: Transmutation works on what she touches. Changing the Celestial Tiamut needed the Uni-Mind, which drew on the other Eternals.

sources.supports: MCU Wiki: Sersi's powers (transmutation, Uni-Mind, regeneration), feats in London, the Amazon and the Emergence, and her limits

feats.claim: Turned a bus into rose petals to protect civilians and turned pavement into sand to trap Kro in London.
Turned a Deviant into a tree in the Amazon, the first time she transmuted a living being.
Turned the Celestial Tiamut to stone through the Uni-Mind.

notableResults.citation: Eternals (2021)
notableResults.note: Through the Uni-Mind she turned the emerging Celestial to stone.

notableResults.citation: Eternals (2021)
notableResults.note: London: her transmutations delayed and redirected Kro; Ikaris drove him off.

conditional.ability: Transmuting a Celestial (and becoming briefly more powerful than one)
conditional.dependsOn: The Uni-Mind with the other Eternals

campaignTags.claim: Eternal regeneration; healed her own stab wound through the Uni-Mind.

unknowns: The largest mass she can transmute at once.
The original claims of a meteor turned to petals and of subduing Ikaris by transmutation are not supported: the MCU Wiki says she never transmuted Ikaris and has no recorded direct fight with him.
Flight and cosmic energy shields are not documented.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe, Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
characters.summary: A master of many martial arts styles who was trained as an assassin from childhood. He inherited the Ten Rings from his father Wenwu and controls them better than Wenwu did: throwing and recalling them, using them as chains, whips, shields and hovering platforms, and combining them with his mother's techniques to make the energy blast that killed the Dweller-in-Darkness.

techniques: Kung fu and other martial arts

mechanisms: Acrobatic evasion; deflected thrown rings with the Dragon Scale Staff
Dragon Scale Armor (Battle of Ta Lo)

weaknesses: Without the Ten Rings he has no ring-granted enhancements and fights as an unpowered, if elite, human martial artist
limitations: His energy powers and enhanced strength and durability come from the Ten Rings, and the Great Protector's boost was temporary

sources.supports: MCU Wiki: Shang-Chi's skills, Ten Rings powers and equipment, and his fights (bus, Macau, Death Dealer, Wenwu, the Dweller-in-Darkness)

feats.claim: Destroyed the Dweller-in-Darkness with a Ten Rings energy blast built on his mother's techniques, helped by Xialing and the Great Protector.
feats.citation: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)

feats.claim: Beat several Ten Rings agents on a moving bus and tricked Razor Fist into cutting the bus in half.
feats.citation: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)

notableResults.citation: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
notableResults.note: Battle of Ta Lo: Shang-Chi gained the upper hand, knocked Wenwu down and took half the rings. The MCU Wiki says it ended in a standstill. The Dweller then took Wenwu, who passed the rings to his son.

notableResults.citation: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
notableResults.note: Team kill with Xialing and the Great Protector.

notableResults.citation: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
notableResults.note: Bus fight in San Francisco: Razor Fist was trapped in the severed rear half of the bus.

notableResults.citation: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
notableResults.note: Nearly beat him in a duel before Wenwu stepped in.

notableResults.citation: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
notableResults.note: Golden Daggers Club in Macau: he was distracted and unwilling to fight, and she won.

conditional.ability: Energy projection, shields, hovering platforms and enhanced physical attributes

unknowns: The origin of the signal the Ten Rings sent at the end of the film.
Appearances after the film were not covered by the page opened.
